Rules / Maintainability

SK7080 The inheritance chain is deeper than the threshold

A class declares more base classes above it, within this compilation's own source, than dotnet_code_quality.SK7080.threshold (default 4).

CategoryMaintainability
Default severityhint
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixno
Language version floor—
Since1.3
SupersedesS110

Why

Every level above a class is a place a member can come from and a place behaviour can be changed without touching the file in front of the reader. The number is worth reporting only for the part of the chain the repository actually wrote: MyControl : Button is one decision somebody made, and the eight framework types above Button are not. So the count stops at the first base class this compilation did not declare — which is also why the default is 4 rather than the textbook 5 or 6, since a chain of four source-declared bases is already unusual. Flattening a hierarchy is a design change with no mechanical form, so there is no fix.

Example

Instead of:

class A { }

class B : A { }

class C : B { }

class D : C { }

class E : D { }   // five source-declared bases above it

Write:

class E {
    readonly A a;      // the same reuse by composition
    readonly B b;
}

When it does not fire

A metric rule has no false positives in the sense doc 16 § R3 means: it reports a measurement against a threshold, and the measurement is either right or a bug. What it can be is useless — a threshold low enough to fire on ordinary code teaches people to switch the category off — so the default is set above what the reference trees contain and the threshold is an .editorconfig option. ⚠ The chain stops at the first base class not declared in this compilation's source. A framework base contributes 1 and its own ancestors contribute nothing: depth from a framework is not a decision anybody in the repository can act on, and counting it would make the rule an opinion about which framework to use. ⚠ The same rule makes the count under-report across an assembly boundary — a base class in a referenced project is metadata here — which is the safe direction and is why the number is described as "within this compilation's own source". ⚠ An unresolved base type withdraws the measurement entirely: a chain that cannot be walked reads as depth 1, and reporting the smaller number would be silent rather than wrong. That is also why the rule produces nothing on a source slice with no dependency closure (issue #277) — the shape is present and the analysis correctly declines. Only classes and record classes are measured; an interface has a graph rather than a chain, and a struct has no base chain to walk. Generated code is excluded. A partial class is reported once, on the part that carries the base list.

Configuration

  • dotnet_code_quality.SK7080.threshold
  • dotnet_diagnostic.SK7080.severity
